annotation.kind: approved source reselection and exact finite formalization of Lemma 3.3 equations (3.10)-(3.11)

assumptions: A and B are real b-by-b matrices; XA, YA, XB, and YB are real b-by-r factors defining Atilde = XA*YA^T and Btilde = YB*XB^T.
XA and XB have orthonormal columns.

Atilde = A + EA and Btilde = B + EB, with ||EA||_F <= epsilon*betaA and ||EB||_F <= epsilon*betaB. This is the paper's approximation hypothesis with an immaterial reversal of the error sign inside a norm.
Unit roundoff u is nonnegative and gamma_c is valid for c = b + 2*r*sqrt(r). The real-valued standard model excludes overflow, underflow, NaNs, and infinities.
The computed product uses exactly one of the two parenthesizations allowed by Lemma 3.3: (XA*(YA^T*YB))*XB^T or XA*((YA^T*YB)*XB^T).
Each of the three ordered matrix products has only its local equation-(2.7) forward error, bounded by gamma of that product's inner dimension times the two input Frobenius norms.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p15_t3_low_rank_matmul_error {b r : Nat} (run : P15LowRankMatMulExecution b r) : let Atilde := p15LowRankMatrix run.XA run.YA; let Btilde := p15LowRankMatrix run.YB run.XB; let gammaC := p15GammaReal (p15LowRankMatMulCost b r) run.unitRoundoff; p15FrobNorm (run.trace.result - p15MatMul Atilde Btilde) <= gammaC * p15FrobNorm Atilde * p15FrobNorm Btilde and p15FrobNorm (run.trace.result - p15MatMul run.A run.B) <= gammaC * p15FrobNorm run.A * p15FrobNorm run.B + run.epsilon * (1 + gammaC) * (run.betaA * p15FrobNorm run.B + p15FrobNorm run.A * run.betaB + run.epsilon * run.betaA * run.betaB)
formal_statement.plain_language: For either permitted three-product evaluation of two low-rank matrices, prove the rounding-error bound (3.10) relative to their low-rank representations and the truncation-plus-rounding bound (3.11) relative to the original matrices.

informal_proof: For either parenthesization, expand the three local equation-(2.7) errors. Orthonormality makes left multiplication by XA and right multiplication by XB^T Frobenius-norm preserving and gives ||XA||_F = ||XB||_F = sqrt(r). Apply triangle and submultiplicative inequalities, first combining gamma_b with gamma_r*sqrt(r) into gamma_(b+r^(3/2)), then combining the final gamma_r*sqrt(r) term into gamma_c for c = b+2*r^(3/2). This proves (3.10). Substitute Atilde=A+EA and Btilde=B+EB, expand EA*B + A*EB + EA*EB, and combine that truncation bound with (3.10) to obtain (3.11).
informal_statement: Lemma 3.3 equations (3.10)-(3.11), including both permitted parenthesizations, the exact c = b+2*r^(3/2) gamma index, and all first- and second-order low-rank approximation terms.
